property_summary: For any state of the contract, C.currentVersion() must return the oracle's currentVersion() with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e., transformed price != raw oracle price for at least some oracle outputs); the mutant that returns the raw oracle.currentVersion() (without transform) will therefore return a different price for any oracle version where payoffDefinition.transform changes the price.

For any oracle version returned, C.currentVersion() returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoff-transformed oracle price; the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() (no transform) will produce a different price for some oracle outputs where the payoff transform changes the price.

For any oracle-reported OracleVersion, C.currentVersion() returns the same OracleVersion but with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() directly will sometimes return an OracleVersion whose price differs (i.e., untransformed) from C.currentVersion(), so there exist oracle prices where the transformed price != raw price.

For any oracle version, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant that returns oracle().currentVersion() directly will sometimes return an untransformed price, so there exists an oracle-reported price where C.currentVersion().price != mutant.currentVersion().price.

For every oracle state, the correct product returns currentVersion() whose price equals the payoff-transformed oracle price; the mutant returns the raw oracle price (no transform) so there exist oracle prices where the two differ.

For any oracle version, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e., transformed(oracle.price)); the mutant wrongly always returns transformed(0) causing a mismatch when oracle.price != 0.

For every oracle price, C.currentVersion() returns oracle().currentVersion() with price equal to payoffDefinition().transform(oraclePrice); the mutant instead returns payoffDefinition().transform(0) so whenever oraclePrice != 0 the returned price differs.

For any oracle version returned by the product's oracle, C.currentVersion() returns that oracle version but with price = payoffDefinition().transform(oracle.price); the mutant instead always returns payoffDefinition().transform(0), so whenever oracle.price != 0 the returned price differs.

For any oracle price p, C.currentVersion() returns oracle().currentVersion() with price == payoffDefinition().transform(p); the mutant returns payoffDefinition().transform(0) instead, so when the oracle's price != 0 the returned price differs.

For every oracle currentVersion returned by the product's oracle, C.currentVersion() forwards that version but with price = payoffDefinition().transform(oraclePrice); the mutant instead returns payoffDefinition().transform(0), so when the oracle's price != 0 the returned price differs.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) always returns the oracle provider's atVersion(id) with its price transformed by the product payoffDefinition (i.e. equals _transform(oracle().atVersion(id))); the mutant returns the raw provider value (no transform) so for some oracle versions where transform changes price the outputs differ.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) must return the provider's oracle version with the product payoffDefinition.transform applied to the price; the mutant returns the raw provider value (no transform) so there exist ids where the price differs.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the product payoffDefinition.transform(...) of the oracle provider's atVersion(id).price; the mutant returns the raw provider price (no transform), so for some oracleVersion ids the returned price differs and thus the equality can be violated.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) must return an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed oracle provider price; the mutant returns the raw provider OracleVersion (no transform) so for some oracleVersion ids the returned price differs and the equality is violated.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the product payoffDefinition.transform(...) of the underlying oracle provider's atVersion(id).price; the mutant returns the provider's raw atVersion without applying transform, so for some oracleVersion ids the returned price will differ and the property is violated.

For any product instance, the public maintenance() getter must return the product's stored maintenance parameter (not the controller's minCollateral); the mutant that returns controller().minCollateral() will differ for any input where controller().minCollateral() != stored maintenance.

For every input, the product's maintenance() view returns its stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returning controller().minCollateral() will differ whenever controller().minCollateral() != the stored maintenance value (the fuzzer will find such inputs).

For any input maintenanceQueryAccount, the correct product returns its stored maintenance parameter via maintenance(account); the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() instead, so whenever the controller's minCollateral != the product's stored maintenance the mutant will return a different value — the test fuzzes these values and asserts equality of maintenance(account) to the stored maintenance by reading both via public getters (maintenance(account) vs maintenance() on the product owner controller), so the buggy mutant will fail for some inputs where they differ.

For any fuzzed controller minCollateral and product stored maintenance, the product.maintenance() getter must return the product's stored maintenance value; the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() so it will differ when those two UFixed18 values are unequal.

For any fuzzed pair of stored product maintenance and controller minCollateral values, the correct product.maintenance(account) view always returns the product's stored maintenance value; the mutant that returns controller().minCollateral() will differ whenever controller.minCollateral() != product's stored maintenance (which the fuzzer can find).

For any deployed C, makerFee() always returns the value stored in the _makerFee storage slot (i.e. equals the contract's configured maker fee); the mutant that reads _takerFee instead will return a different value whenever makerFee != takerFee, so the property is violated for those inputs.

For any configured product, makerFee() returns the stored maker fee; the mutant that reads _takerFee instead will produce a different returned UFixed18 whenever makerFee != takerFee, so there exist fuzzed fee values that make the mutant differ.

For any pair of stored fees, makerFee() returns the value stored in the makerFee slot; the mutant that reads the takerFee slot will return a different value whenever makerFee != takerFee, so there exist fuzz inputs (makerFee, takerFee) that make the mutant differ.

For any stored maker and taker fee values, makerFee() returns the value stored in the makerFee slot; the mutant that reads the takerFee slot instead will return a different value whenever makerFee != takerFee, so there exist fuzzed fee pairs that make the mutant produce a different return value.

For any pair of makerFee and takerFee stored in the contract, makerFee() must return the value stored in the makerFee storage slot; the mutant returns the takerFee slot value instead, so when makerFee != takerFee the mutant returns a different value.

For every stored taker fee value in the contract, the takerFee() getter must return exactly that stored UFixed18 value (i.e., it is idempotent / returns the stored fee), whereas the mutant doubles the stored value and thus will return a different (2x) value for some fuzzed stored fee.
